question.text:
A computer system supports a logical address space of $2^{44}$ bytes. It uses inverted paging with a page size of $\mathbf{8 1 9 2}$ bytes. A logical address is divided into a $\mathbf{3 1}$-bit logical page number, a $\mathbf{25}-bit process id, and $\mathbf{8}$ control bits. The system has $\mathbf{16 ~GB}$ of physical memory. Each entry of the inverted page table uses eight bytes. All the pages in the system have the same size.

The size of the inverted page table in $\mathrm{MB}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ . (Answer in integer)
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
A computer system supports a logical address space of $2^{45}$ bytes. It uses a three-level hierarchical paging scheme with a page size of $\mathbf{16 ~KB}$ $(2^{14}$ bytes$)$. A logical address is divided into a $b$-bit index to the top-level page table, a middle-level index, an inner-level index, and a page offset.

Each entry in all levels of the page tables uses $\mathbf{8}$ bytes. In this system, every page table at every level fits exactly within one single page.

The value of $b$ is:

  1. $7$
     
  2. $9$
     
  3. $11$
     
  4. $13$
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider a system where each process has a maximum need of $\mathbf{4}$ instances of a specific resource type. The system has a total of $\mathbf{13}$ instances of this resource available.

What is the largest number of processes $(N)$ that the system can support to always avoid deadlock?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider a system with $\mathbf{4}$ processes $(P_1, P_2, P_3, P_4)$ and $\mathbf{10}$ instances of a resource. $P_1$ has a maximum need of $\mathbf{3}$ instances, and $P_2$ has a maximum need of $\mathbf{4}$ instances. $P_3$ and $P_4$ both have the same maximum need of $\mathbf{K}$ instances.

The largest integer value of $\mathbf{K}$ that will always avoid deadlock is:

question.text:
Consider a system with $\mathbf{5}$ processes that share $\mathbf{12}$ instances of the same resource type. Each process can request a maximum of $\mathbf{K}$ instances. Resources can be requested and released only one at a time.

The largest value of $\mathbf{K}$ that will always avoid deadlock is:
